correctness.rationale: The sixteen exceptional classes are reconstructed in the blow-up basis. Exact intersections give a 5-regular triangle-free graph with 40 double points, hence \(\chi(W)=16\cdot2-40=-8\). Since the degree-4 del Pezzo surface has \(\chi(X)=8\), additivity gives \(\chi(Y)=16\). The finite map to the complement of the discriminant conic makes \(Y\) affine; as a smooth affine complex surface it has finite CW dimension at most \(2\). With the published \(H_1(Y,\mathbf Z)\cong\mathbf Z^{10}\), this forces free \(H_2(Y,\mathbf Z)\cong\mathbf Z^{25}\) and no higher homology. The published \(H_2(\pi_1Y,\mathbf Z)\cong\mathbf Z^{25}\) then makes the Hopf surjection an isomorphism.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper computes \(H_1(Y,\mathbf Z)\) and \(H_2(\pi_1Y,\mathbf Z)\), but the latter is explicitly group homology obtained from Hopf's formula for a presentation. It does not state \(H_2(Y,\mathbf Z)\), \(\chi(Y)=16\), the full ordinary homology, or the Hopf-map isomorphism. Exact and alias searches for those geometric invariants found no covering statement. The prior same-source ledger finding concerns normalization of the wobbly divisor for \(n\ge3\), whereas this result concerns ordinary homology of its complement only for \(n=2\).

value.rationale: The initiating paper is explicitly motivated by topology of the very-stable locus but leaves a sharp distinction between ordinary homology of the space and group homology of its fundamental group. The result closes that gap in the geometrically distinguished surface case by giving the complete integral homology and showing that the Hopf map is an isomorphism. This supplies a compact topological profile of a central moduli-theoretic complement rather than an arbitrary numerical invariant.
